# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We want Simplicity, the project and the community around it, to be a welcoming, harassment-free space for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

## Our standards

Behaviour that helps:

- being kind, patient and respectful of different viewpoints and experiences,
- giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback,
- taking responsibility for mistakes and learning from them,
- focusing on what is best for the community.

Behaviour that is not acceptable:

- sexualised language or imagery, and unwelcome sexual attention,
- trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks,
- public or private harassment,
- publishing other people's private information without their explicit permission,
- anything else that would reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies in all project spaces (issues, pull requests, discussions, reviews) and when someone represents the project in public. Writing published on the Simplicity site is also covered by the [community guidelines](https://simplicity.akadeepesh.com/guidelines).

## Enforcement

Report unacceptable behaviour privately to the maintainer, [@akadeepesh](https://github.com/akadeepesh), using the contact details on [akadeepesh.com](https://akadeepesh.com). Every report is reviewed promptly and kept confidential.

The maintainer may remove, edit or reject comments, commits, code, issues and other contributions that break this Code of Conduct, and may temporarily or permanently ban anyone whose behaviour is inappropriate, threatening or harmful.
